$comment: Shared twin case table for openbindings.openapi@1 §9.2: what a form part whose resolved Schema Object declares no `type` defaults to, per accepted OAS edition. The admitted/refused half of every cell is derived from the pinned OAS bytes and is portable meaning; the emission string is a pinned rendering of each engine, normalized so that an omitted per-part Content-Type header and an explicit text/plain one read alike ([RFC7578] Section 4.4 permits both). Every harness executing this table renders the case as a WHOLE OpenAPI document and loads it through its own engine's shipped loader; a cell whose document does not load at all decides `source-refused`. A boolean-literal part schema is deliberately absent — see the generator's header. UPDATED 2026-08-17: the urlencoded rows of 3.0.0, 3.0.1, 3.0.2 and 3.0.3 moved. Until then a legacyOpenAPIFormEncoding predicate in all three engines put those four editions' control-free urlencoded parts on the RFC6570-style path, where the Encoding Object's default contentType table was never consulted; their object-valued cells emitted the object's own members (k=v) instead of its JSON image. Each of those editions' own §4.1 tells tooling to make no distinction between the patch versions of the 3.0 line, and 3.0.4 — a 3.0.* version — states that with all three RFC6570-style fields absent "Encoding is to be based on contentType alone", so the predicate was deleted (ruling: design/openapi-30-urlencoded-default-lane-ruling.md; specification: openbindings.openapi@1 §2 and §9.2). The 3.0/3.1 split this table exists for is unaffected: it is a LINE split each line's own text states, not a patch split. Generated by corpus-lab/scripts/build-part-default-type-absent-table.mjs; edit that script, not this file.

cases.name: 3.1.0|multipart|declared-string
cases.basis: control. OAS 3.1.0 §4.8.15.1's Encoding Object `contentType` sentence closes with "for all other cases the default is application/octet-stream", which read alone would reach a declared `string`. It does not: §4.8.15.2, that same object's own example, annotates `id: {type: string, format: uuid}` with "# default is text/plain". The clause is the residue of the 3.0-line sentence's dropped primitive clauses (3.0.3 states "for other primitive types – text/plain" and closes with no catch-all), and 3.1.1 — a patch release per its Appendix A — tabulates text/plain again. §4.8.14.5 states the answer for this lane outright ("If the property is a primitive, or an array of primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain", reserving application/octet-stream for a `type: string` WITH a `contentEncoding`), and its worked example resolves an inner `type: string` to text/plain.

cases.name: 3.1.0|urlencoded|declared-string
cases.basis: control. §4.8.14.5's list is scoped to `multipart` and does not reach this lane. OAS 3.1.0 §4.8.15.1's Encoding Object `contentType` sentence closes with "for all other cases the default is application/octet-stream", which read alone would reach a declared `string`. It does not: §4.8.15.2, that same object's own example, annotates `id: {type: string, format: uuid}` with "# default is text/plain". The clause is the residue of the 3.0-line sentence's dropped primitive clauses (3.0.3 states "for other primitive types – text/plain" and closes with no catch-all), and 3.1.1 — a patch release per its Appendix A — tabulates text/plain again. That sentence is one field description keyed on the property type alone, so it resolves the same in both lanes. 3.1.0 does consult it here, because it carries "If a value is explicitly defined, then the value of contentType (implicit or explicit) SHALL be ignored" on each of style, explode and allowReserved, which puts a control-free urlencoded property on the content lane.
